title: What Do Africans Think of Trump’s Travel Ban List?
desc: The restrictions on half the continent have been called racist and unfair. “We don’t come to the United States because we’re running away,” one N.B.A. fan said.

title: Saudi Arabia’s MBS speaks with Trump regularly, urges harsh actions against Iran: Report
desc: Reports indicate Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman is maintaining regular contact with President Trump, privately urging decisive military action against Iran to "cut off the head of the snake" and neutralize its regional influence.

title: Father's smoking addiction can increase child's diabetes risk, warns study
desc: Smoking Is injurious to health, so we know. But a new study hints that fathers’ nicotine use might impact how their children process sugar. Changes in insulin, glucose, and liver function could raise the risk of diabetes.

title: Kiambu: DCI Nabs 2 Suspects Including Nigerian Linked to Narcotics Smuggling Network
desc: Detectives in Kiambu arrest two suspects, including a Nigerian, linked to a narcotics smuggling network. Key evidence seized during intelligence-led operations.

title: In ‘The Lady,’ a Current Royal Scandal Meets an Older One
desc: The series, “inspired” by the story of a royal dresser later convicted of murder, is getting added attention over the former Duchess of York’s ties to Jeffrey Epstein.

title: Quartz Countertop Makers Want Immunity Against Legal Claims from Sick Stone Cutters
desc: Workers are filing lawsuits against the countertop industry as cases of silicosis, a deadly lung disease, rise.

title: Iran war is making it harder for the Federal Reserve to cut interest rates
desc: Some economists think the Fed, facing inflationary pressures from rising energy prices, may not cut interest rates at all this year.

title: Former NUP aspirants seek audience with Museveni
desc: The group of 13 former NUP political aspirants from the Lango sub-region claim that NRM persuaded them to withdraw their candidature for various leadership positions, leaving the ruling party’s candidates to win the races unopposed.
